title: Faking numbers and learning music from Manetta
summary: He learned tunes quickly by ear. His teacher Manetta also set him on his first professional job.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: But when he played these numbers that he wrote himself, like Mom is Gone Goodbye and those kind of numbers, did you use music for that?
You were faking them? Yeah. He would teach you the numbers of the band you played with?

Yeah, well I was quick on that. I would always follow them. I didn't care what they played. I knew it was progressive pretty well. I was having trouble. That's another thing that they liked. Anything they played, most likely I could play whether I knew it or not, it was progressive, unless it was a difficult number like Body and Soul or something like that. But you did learn some songs from music. Oh, getting to your eyes, numbers like that, I might have to hear the music, but just a little round number, whatever, I didn't worry about nothing like that. Mario Minera was the one who taught you to music? Yeah, he taught me. And he was the one who gave me the first job. The first job I would play with professionals. There was more of a four pieces to that, to a halfway house back at the Mel Street. I taught them.
I know they gave you this job.
Yeah, he gave me. He set me on that job. I don't remember who the musicians was at the time, but he set me on that job.
